answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by locked stake, so splitting funds across a plume of accounts does not multiply voting power or payouts. To overwhelm the system, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying opportunity cost and often moving the market price; a river of cheap identities cannot evade that constraint, while an ember of stake earns only ember-sized influence.
